# AMZN — Technical & Trend Analysis
**As of the close of 2026-09-04 · Last price $258.51**

---

## 1. Data integrity note

I pulled the full daily series (192 sessions, 2025-12-01 → 2026-09-04) and the verified snapshot for 2026-09-04. The two sources are **fully consistent**: the latest row is O 259.07 / H 261.12 / L 255.29 / C 258.51 / V 30,749,900, and every indicator value returned by `get_indicators` matches the snapshot to the decimal (e.g., 50-SMA 253.9494, RSI 49.5491, MACD 0.3392). **No discrepancy to flag.** All figures below are drawn from those two tool outputs; any percentage I quote is simple arithmetic between two explicitly dated prices.

*(The snapshot also returns an `mfi` of 0.4888 on a 0–1 scale; because the scaling convention is ambiguous and MFI is outside the selected set, I have not used it.)*

---

## 2. Price structure — what actually happened

**The regime is: a completed post-earnings impulse, followed by a controlled six-week retracement that is now trying to stabilize.**

Key anchors from the verified data:

| Date | Event | Price |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-29 | Pullback low close (pre-earnings) | 226.65 |
| 2026-07-30 | Volume 101.8M, close 235.50 (event eve) | 235.50 |
| 2026-07-31 | **Gap-up open 265.00** vs prior close 235.50; close 271.58 on 129.1M | 271.58 |
| 2026-08-03 | Impulse peak: intraday high **287.20**, close 284.02 on 90.8M | 284.02 |
| 2026-08-18 | First pullback low close | 259.45 |
| 2026-08-28 | Lower-high rally: high 267.56, close 266.43 on 49.5M — **immediately rejected** | 266.43 |
| 2026-09-01 | Pullback low: intraday **251.93**, close 254.92 | 254.92 |
| 2026-09-04 | Close 258.51; high 261.12 faded into the close | 258.51 |

Three structural facts matter:

1. **The 7/31 gap is still unfilled.** The void runs from 235.50 (7/30 close) to 265.00 (7/31 open). At 258.51 AMZN is sitting *inside* that gap, in its upper half. Nothing about the price action since 8/3 has repaired or negated that gap — it is a large, unresolved structural feature.
2. **Since 8/3, the sequence of highs and lows is descending:** highs 287.20 (8/3) → 278.84 (8/11) → 267.56 (8/28); lows 257.73 (8/18) → 251.93 (9/1). That is a textbook short-term downtrend nested inside a medium-term uptrend.
3. **The retracement has been orderly, not distributive.** Measured from the 8/3 close (284.02) to the 9/4 close (258.51), the decline is **−8.98%**. Measured from the 8/3 intraday high (287.20) to the 9/1 intraday low (251.93), it is **−12.28%**. Against the pre-earnings close of 226.65 (7/29), AMZN is still **+14.06%**. So this is a give-back of part of an impulse, not a trend break.

A useful confluence exercise: the post-gap range 235.50 → 287.20 is 51.70 points. The **50% retracement sits at 261.35** — which lands almost exactly on the 20-day Bollinger basis of **262.20**. The 61.8% retracement is 255.25, and the 9/1 low (251.93) marked a ~68% retracement. In other words, the entire "support/resistance" debate is happening inside a single, well-defined retracement ladder.

---

## 3. Why these eight indicators

This is a **post-impulse consolidation inside a confirmed primary uptrend**, with volatility collapsing. That regime needs (a) multi-horizon trend structure to separate "pullback" from "reversal," (b) a momentum oscillator that isn't already saturated, (c) a band/volatility model to frame the compressed range, and (d) a volume cross-check because the whole move was volume-driven (earnings gaps).

| # | Indicator | Role in this specific setup |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `close_10_ema` | Detects whether the short-term down-swing has actually stopped; price is currently pinned to it (−0.24%). |
| 2 | `close_50_sma` | Defines the swing-trend line and has *not been closed below* since 7/30 — the cleanest invalidation level. |
| 3 | `close_200_sma` | Confirms the strategic trend and the golden-cross regime; both averages are rising. |
| 4 | `macd` | Measures whether the pullback has eroded the underlying positive momentum (still > 0, but fading fast). |
| 5 | `rsi` | At 49.5 it is genuinely neutral — no overbought/oversold distortion, so it can register the *next* divergence. |
| 6 | `boll` (+`boll_ub`/`boll_lb`) | The ±2σ envelope has compressed violently (29.6% → 8.7% of basis); this is the best available breakout bracket. |
| 7 | `atr` | Volatility has contracted from 9.98 to 6.69 — directly sets stop distance and position size. |
| 8 | `vwma` | The gap move was volume-driven; VWMA tells us whether holders are in profit at current prices. |

I deliberately avoided pairing RSI with a second oscillator, and I did not add a third MACD parameter set — the histogram (macd − macds = −1.179) is fully implied by the MACD pair and adding it would be redundant.

---

## 4. Trend: bullish primary, bearish intermediate, flattening short-term

**Long-term (200-SMA): intact and rising.**
`close_200_sma` = **239.12**, up from 238.68 on 8/28 and 234.75 on 7/30. It has been rising continuously for the entire visible window. Price is **+8.11%** above it — a healthy premium with no extension extreme. The 50-SMA (253.95) sits **14.83 points (+6.2%) above** the 200-SMA, so the golden-cross configuration is intact and the spread is *widening*, not compressing.

**Medium-term (50-SMA): the line in the sand.**
`close_50_sma` = **253.95**, up from 251.66 on 8/28 and 246.38 on 7/30 — a steady, positive slope. Critically: **AMZN has not closed a single session below its 50-SMA since 7/30** (the last sub-50-SMA close was 235.50 on 7/30, before the gap). Even during the 9/1 washout, the close of 254.92 held above the then-50-SMA of 252.41. That is the strongest single piece of evidence that this is a retracement, not a distribution top.

**Short-term (10-EMA): flattening at the scene of the crime.**
`close_10_ema` = **259.14**, down from its 8/12 peak of 267.18, but the *rate* of decline has collapsed: −0.97 on 9/1, −0.08 on 9/2, −0.08 on 9/3, −0.14 on 9/4. The close (258.51) is **0.24% below** it. Flat 10-EMA + price straddling it = the down-move has lost its driving force, but buyers have not yet taken control.

**Interpretation:** the three averages are stacked bullishly (price 258.51 > 50-SMA 253.95 > 200-SMA 239.12), but price is *below* its own 10-EMA. That is the classic signature of a pullback in an uptrend that has bottomed in *time* but not yet in *confirmation*.

---

## 5. Momentum: decay is decelerating

**MACD is the most informative indicator on the board right now.**

- `macd` peaked at **8.432 on 8/11** and has bled to **0.339 on 9/4**.
- `macds` (signal) peaked at **6.217 on 8/14**; it is now **1.519**.
- The bearish crossover occurred when the histogram flipped negative on **8/17** (−0.310).
- The histogram bottomed at **−1.683 on 8/27** and has now improved for three consecutive sessions: −1.585 (9/2) → −1.354 (9/3) → **−1.179 (9/4)**.

Two things follow. First, the **MACD line is still above zero** — a bearish crossover *in positive territory* is, mechanically, a pullback signal rather than a trend-reversal signal. Second, the **histogram is contracting from below**, which is the earliest objective evidence that selling pressure is exhausting. The actionable warning: MACD is only **0.34 above the zero line**. A cross below zero in the coming sessions would materially downgrade the medium-term picture and would likely coincide with a 50-SMA breach.

**RSI is neutral and, importantly, unsullied.**

`rsi` = **49.55**, essentially dead-center. The path is revealing:
- 72.23 on 8/3 (the impulse peak — mildly overbought, never extreme)
- 65.87 on 8/10, 55.64 on 8/19, 55.85 on 8/28 — a clean sequence of **lower RSI highs**, confirming the descending price highs
- 46.33 on 9/1 (pullback low), then 49.90 / 49.55 on 9/3–9/4

I want to be precise here: **there is no confirmed bullish RSI divergence.** The 9/1 price low (251.93) came with an RSI low (46.33) that was *lower* than the 8/27 reading (47.23) alongside a *lower* price — that is confirmation, not divergence. What we have instead is a simple recovery off sub-50. The bullish case would strengthen on an RSI push through **56** (the ceiling of the last two rallies) accompanied by a price close above 262.

---

## 6. Volatility: an extremely compressed spring

This is the most striking feature of the chart.

**Bollinger envelope (±2σ around the 20-SMA):**
- Basis (`boll`): **262.20**
- Upper (`boll_ub`): **273.63**
- Lower (`boll_lb`): **250.76**
- Width: **22.87 points = 8.72% of the basis**

Now compare with 8/19, when the bands were at their widest: UB 296.99, LB 220.47, width **76.53 = 29.6% of basis**. The envelope has compressed to roughly **30% of its August peak width** in twelve sessions. That is a dramatic volatility contraction.

Two mechanical consequences:
1. **The bands are now a genuine bracket.** With the lower band at 250.76 and the 9/1 low at 251.93, there is tight confluence beneath the market. The upper band at 273.63 coincides roughly with the 8/10–8/11 congestion (278 area). A close outside either edge after this degree of compression would be a high-information event.
2. **The lower band is rising fast** (215.57 on 8/10 → 250.76 on 9/4), which is the signature of a basis rolling over while price holds — i.e., the band is coming up to meet the price rather than the price collapsing to meet the band. That is a *constructive* geometry.

**ATR (14):** **6.69**, or **2.59% of the close**. It has fallen from **9.98 on 8/5** and **7.25 on 9/1**. This is a direct, quantified argument for *tighter* stops and *larger* position size than three weeks ago — and it also means that a 1×ATR stop (≈$6.7) is now too tight for a swing thesis given the 8/28–9/1 whipsaw range (high 267.56 → low 251.93 = 15.63 points, or 2.3 ATR).

---

## 7. Volume: the pullback is not being distributed

Raw volume recently versus the August impulse:

| Date | Close | Volume | Read |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-03 | 284.02 | 90.8M | Peak-price, heavy participation |
| 2026-08-28 | 266.43 | 49.5M | Up-day on rising volume, but rejected at 267.56 |
| 2026-08-31 | 259.77 | 46.1M | Down −2.5%, elevated volume — the day's only real distribution print |
| 2026-09-01 | 254.92 | 31.7M | Down, volume *falling* |
| 2026-09-02 | 254.98 | 24.0M | Lowest volume of the sequence; price held |
| 2026-09-03 | 258.90 | 26.9M | Up on light volume |
| 2026-09-04 | 258.51 | 30.7M | Up on moderate volume, but closed near session low of range |

The pattern is **volume drying up into the low** — 24.0M on 9/2 vs 90.8M on 8/3. That is the behavior of a market where sellers have run out of urgency, not one where institutions are exiting. The blemish is 8/31, and the 9/4 intraday fade (high 261.12 → close 258.51) shows supply still sitting near 261.

**VWMA: 259.78.** Price at 258.51 is **0.49% below** the volume-weighted average — marginally negative, meaning the average dollar of recent volume is a hair underwater. But note the VWMA is falling rapidly (272.05 on 8/20 → 259.78 on 9/4) and is *converging on price*, not diverging above it. Concretely: VWMA (259.78), 10-EMA (259.14), and the 9/3–9/4 closes (258.90, 258.51) are all inside a **1.3-point band**. The market has found a volume-weighted equilibrium in the 258.5–260 zone. That is a coiled, decision-ready condition.

---

## 8. Level map (all values from verified 2026-09-04 data)

**Resistance — layered and close overhead**
- **259.14–259.78** — 10-EMA / VWMA (immediate; price is inside it)
- **260.11–262.20** — 8/20 close, 9/4 high (261.12), **20-SMA/Bollinger basis 262.20**, and the 50% retracement of the post-gap range (261.35). This is the single most important zone on the chart.
- **265.00–267.56** — top of the 7/31 gap (265.00) and the 8/28 rejection high (267.56)
- **273.63** — upper Bollinger band
- **278.00–278.84** — 8/3 open / 8/11 high congestion
- **287.20** — 2026 high (8/3 intraday)

**Support — three tiers**
- **253.95** — 50-SMA (never closed below since 7/30). First warning line.
- **250.76–251.93** — lower Bollinger band + 9/1 low. This is the structural floor of the post-earnings consolidation.
- **245.2–246.0** — June congestion (6/15 close 246.02, 6/16 close 246.00, 6/9 close 244.19)
- **239.12** — 200-SMA

---

## 9. Actionable plan

**Bias: neutral-to-constructive. The primary trend is up, the pullback is mature, but confirmation has not yet printed.** The current price sits mid-range between 250.76 and 273.63, which is the worst risk/reward location on the chart. Do not chase here.

### Scenario A — Bullish confirmation (base case, ~55% weight)
**Trigger:** a daily close **above 262.20** (20-SMA) with volume ≥ 40M, ideally with RSI > 56 and MACD histogram crossing back above zero.
- Entry: 262.50–263.50
- Stop: **251.00** (below the 9/1 low of 251.93 and the lower band of 250.76) = ~11 points ≈ 1.6× ATR
- Target 1: **266.50–267.56** (8/28 high) — partial exit
- Target 2: **273.63** (upper band) — R:R ≈ 1.0 from entry 262.50
- Target 3: **287.20** (2026 high) — R:R ≈ 2.2
- Note: T1 is close, so scale rather than take the whole position off; the asymmetric payoff is in T3.

### Scenario B — Range / coil resolution (needs patience)
If price continues to oscillate between **250.76 and 267.56**, the correct posture is to trade the edges, not the middle:
- Long at **252–254** (lower band + 9/1 low + just above the 50-SMA), stop **249.50** (below the band, ~2.4 points ≈ 0.4 ATR — too tight; use **248.00**, ≈1× ATR below entry), target 261.50–262.20.
- Short/trim at **266–267.50**, stop **270.50** (above the 8/28 high plus ~1 ATR), target 259–260. This is a counter-trend trade and should be sized smaller.

### Scenario C — Bearish invalidation (~20% weight)
**Triggers, in order of severity:**
1. Daily close **below 253.95** (50-SMA) — first crack; reduce long exposure.
2. Daily close **below 250.76** (lower Bollinger band) — post-earnings structure broken; next objectives 245–246, then 239.12 (200-SMA).
3. **MACD crossing below zero** (currently only 0.34 above it) — would likely front-run #1 and is the fastest early warning.

### Risk management
- ATR is **6.69 (2.59%)** and falling. A 1.5–2.0× ATR stop is now 10–13.4 points. Set position size so that a full stop-out costs ≤1% of equity: at an 11-point stop, that is roughly 0.09% of equity per share of notional — i.e., size on *risk*, not on dollar value.
- Avoid holding size into the next earnings event: the historical evidence in this dataset is that AMZN's earnings gaps are violent and immediate (2/4 close 232.99 → 2/6 close 210.32 across two sessions on 179.2M volume; and 7/30 close 235.50 → 7/31 close 271.58). Indicator-based stops do **not** protect across a gap.
- Because Bollinger width has compressed to 8.72% of basis, expect a **volatility expansion** — direction unknown. Consider a bracket approach (break of 262.20 or 250.76) rather than a directional guess.

---

## 10. What would change my mind

# AMZN Company News Review — 2026-08-28 through 2026-09-03 (America/New_York)

## Scope and evidence quality

- The frozen feed contains **20 supplied records out of 202 eligible unique records**, so this is a roughly 10% sample and is not guaranteed exhaustive.
- The supplied items are **headlines and vendor summaries, not full articles**. I cannot verify details omitted from the summaries, including Amazon’s response to the strike, the scope of the Justice Department review, analyst rating/price-target changes, or underlying financial estimates.
- No supplied records are dated **Aug 28–Sep 1 ET**. The supplied coverage is concentrated on **Sep 3 ET**, with one article published at 03:17 UTC on Sep 4, which is **23:17 ET on Sep 3** and therefore inside the window. The absence of earlier-week items is a coverage limitation, not evidence that no news occurred.
- Several records are not AMZN-specific or are generic market/peer commentary. They are treated as sector context only.

## Bottom line for AMZN

The supplied news set contains **no clear, company-specific fundamental surprise** that would independently justify a large re-rating. The tone is mildly positive from the broad Magnificent Seven rally and AI-cloud narrative, but that is partly offset by:

1. A localized but negative **labor headline** at Amazon’s Riverside, California warehouse.
2. A widening **beef-pricing review** that includes Amazon among contacted retailers.
3. Continued debate over **AI capex and costly spending cycles**, which is a sector-wide overhang.

For the **Sep 4 session**, broad macro news—especially the jobs report referenced by the Sep 3 preview—is likely to dominate. AMZN-specific headlines look more like modest sentiment and headline-risk items than standalone drivers.

---

## Material AMZN-specific developments

### 1. One-day warehouse strike in Riverside, California — modest negative, low near-term financial materiality

At **19:08:55 ET on Sep 3** (23:08:55 UTC), Yahoo published a report stating that on **Sep 2, 2026**, Amazon workers represented by **Teamsters Local 1932** at the **DJT6 warehouse in Riverside, California** held a **one-day unfair labor practice strike**. The summary says workers alleged **illegal retaliation** and **refusal to recognize the union** at one of Amazon’s largest U.S. logistics hubs.  
Source: Yahoo — [“What Amazon.com (AMZN)'s Riverside Warehouse Strike Reveals About Labor Risk in Its Logistics Model”](https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=9ef8cb261c6771c2ee299a911af12007853d7b8869a2027e0e2995a35ac1dd44)

**Likely impact:** Slightly negative for AMZN sentiment, primarily as a **labor-relations and operating-risk headline**. A one-day strike at a single hub is unlikely to be financially material on its own. The more important medium-term issue is whether the action signals broader unionization pressure or recurring disruption across Amazon’s logistics network.

**Horizon:** Immediate headline risk over 1–3 days; medium-term risk over 1–3 months if labor actions spread.

**Uncertainty:** High. The summary does not quantify lost throughput, strike participation, cost, or Amazon’s response. The evidence is headline/summary-level only.

---

### 2. Justice Department beef-pricing review widens; Amazon among retailers contacted — slight negative headline risk, likely immaterial near term

At **17:28:13 ET on Sep 3**, Yahoo reported that the Justice Department widened a beef-pricing review and that officials contacted **eight retailers, including Walmart, Costco, and Amazon**, amid record beef prices.  
Source: Yahoo — [“Walmart Jumps Nearly 2.8% as Justice Department Widens Beef-Pricing Review”](https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=a0271895d125cf03a744e6d2891541b2717b9dcc817bf83b32a9e9d789b46de6)

**Likely impact:** Slightly negative regulatory/headline risk for AMZN, but probably immaterial to earnings unless the review expands into formal allegations or enforcement. The same headline notes Walmart rose nearly 2.8%, which conflicts with a simple “negative for retailers” read-across and suggests the market did not treat the news as broadly punitive.

**Horizon:** Low immediate impact; potential medium-term headline risk if Amazon is named more specifically.

**Uncertainty:** High. The summary does not describe what information was requested, whether Amazon is a focus, or what potential remedies are under discussion.

---

### 3. “Amazon vs. Microsoft” AI-cloud comparison — modest positive narrative, but opinion rather than new data

At **17:13 ET on Sep 3**, Yahoo published a comparison arguing that Amazon’s revenue growth may be slower than Microsoft’s but is **accelerating quickly**, and framed the contest around which is the superior AI-cloud stock.  
Source: Yahoo — [“Amazon vs. Microsoft: 1 Key Metric Identifies the Superior Artificial Intelligence (AI) Cloud Stock”](https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=3413ec929cf8b8d3bbeafd6ee9b96378ac8cfe451773cf8204bf8f5c4b564066)

**Likely impact:** Mildly positive for AMZN sentiment because it reinforces the **AWS/AI cloud growth narrative** and pushes back against the view that Amazon is losing the AI-cloud race. However, this is an analytical/opinion piece, not a company disclosure or estimate revision.

**Horizon:** 1–4 weeks, mostly through sentiment and multiple support rather than near-term earnings revisions.

**Uncertainty:** High. The summary does not identify the “one key metric,” provide specific AWS growth figures, or include any rating or price-target change.

---

### 4. “Top Analyst Reports for Amazon, AbbVie & Alibaba” — mixed; highlights AI investment and costly spending

At **16:52 ET on Sep 3**, Yahoo published a piece grouping Amazon with AbbVie and Alibaba and referring to “contrasting growth drivers and challenges, from AI investment and drug launches to costly spending cycles.”  
Source: Yahoo — [“Top Analyst Reports for Amazon, AbbVie & Alibaba”](https://finnhub.io/api/news?id=b0804b234e511e69808b38f92c6ee8ffc81d307ea5abe364d75d67f8e8966f56)

**Likely impact:** Mixed. The reference to **AI investment and costly spending cycles** reinforces the bear case around capex intensity and free-cash-flow pressure. But the summary does not disclose a specific AMZN rating change, price target, or estimate revision, so its direct trading signal is weak.

**Horizon:** 1–4 weeks, mainly as part of the ongoing AI-capex debate.

**Uncertainty:** High. The summary does not attribute specific claims or ratings to AMZN versus the other named companies.

---

### 5. Amazon vs. Disney consumer-stock comparison — quality positive, valuation debate neutral

At **23:17:44 ET on Sep 3** — published as 03:17 UTC on Sep 4 but still inside the Sep 3 ET calendar day — Yahoo published a comparison stating that **Amazon’s cloud dominance and 10.8% net margin** contrast with **Disney’s lower valuation multiples and stronger free cash flow**.

## 1. Executive Summary

AMZN is in the middle of the most aggressive capital-deployment cycle in its history, and the Q2 2026 numbers show both the payoff and the cost:

- **Revenue re-accelerated hard.** H1 2026 revenue reached **$382,125M** (+18.2% y/y), with Q2 2026 at **$200,606M (+19.6% y/y)** and Q1 2026 at **$181,519M (+16.6% y/y)** — a marked step-up from the low-teens growth of 2025.
- **Operating leverage is real.** Q2 2026 operating income **$27,461M**, a **13.7% margin** vs. 11.4% a year ago (+230bp). H1 operating margin 13.4% vs. 11.6%. Gross margin improved to 52.3% (Q2'25: 51.8%) while operating expense fell to 38.6% of revenue from 40.4%.
- **BUT headline EPS is heavily distorted.** Q2 2026 net income of **$62,647M** (EPS $5.75) includes a **$50,486M pre-tax upward revaluation of equity securities without a readily determinable fair value** (and $12,328M in Q1 2026; **$62,814M for H1**). This non-cash mark flows through non-operating income. **Stripping it out, Q2 2026 core EPS is ≈$2.16 vs. $1.68 (+~29%)** — strong, but nowhere near the +242% GAAP optics.
- **Free cash flow has turned negative.** TTM operating cash flow **$161,403M (+33% y/y)** was more than absorbed by TTM capex of **$173,028M (+61% y/y)** → **TTM FCF of –$11,625M**, versus +$13,481M a year earlier. H1 2026 FCF was **–$26,992M**.

**Verdict framing:** Fundamentally AMZN is *operationally* accelerating (revenue, margin, cash generation), but *financially* it is now a capex-intensive, levered, negative-FCF business whose reported earnings contain a very large non-cash mark. Traders must separate the two.

That is operating leverage outrunning depreciation, and it is the single hardest fact in the debate to explain away.

The bear's strongest ground was capital intensity and the balance-sheet trajectory, and it deserves real weight: capex went $44.2B → $54.2B sequentially (not flattening, which directly punctures the bull's "if capex merely flattens, FCF inflects" conditional), capex is 27% of revenue and 2.3x TTM D&A, gross debt rose 92% to $132.2B in six months, interest expense rose 155% and flipped to net interest expense, and the quick ratio is 0.875. Its 32x core TTM EPS claim is arithmetically fair, but it prices 32x against core EPS growing ~29% — roughly a 1.1x PEG on an accelerating, margin-expanding franchise. **Executive Summary**: AMZN is Overweight, but built in stages and capped at 1.0x standard allocation until the Q3 print confirms the capex and depreciation trajectory. Stage 1: ~0.30x at 252.00–254.50 (lower band / 9-1 low / just above the rising 50-SMA at 253.95), sized off a realistic stress stop near 248.00 rather than the idealized 2.74-point gap to the 250.76 daily-close invalidation. Stage 2: ~0.30x only on a daily close above 262.20 on ≥40M shares with a next-session hold above 259.78–262.20; Stage 3: ~0.20x only after a confirmed break-and-retest above 267.56 alongside capex or AWS segment confirmation. Do not add at 267.75 into the 267.56 trim zone — treat 267.56 and 273.63 as partial scale-out levels, keep total single-name drawdown at ≤2% of portfolio value, cut to market weight on a daily close below 250.76, reduce to Underweight below 245.00, and never average down. Horizon 3–6 months, re-scored on the Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction goes with the operating evidence; size, entry geometry and add discipline go with the neutral analyst, whose corrections no one rebutted.

What the aggressive analyst won, unrefuted by either colleague: AMZN grew Q2 revenue +19.6% (accelerating from +16.6%), operating income +43.2% to $27.5B, operating margin +230bp to 13.7%, and TTM operating cash flow +33.2% to $161.4B — with inventory flat at $38.2B, marketing +2.5% against +19.6% revenue, and SBC down to 3.0% of revenue. Margins expanded while D&A was already running +31% y/y and capex was at peak intensity, which is operating leverage outrunning depreciation, and it is the hardest fact in the debate to explain away. On valuation, ~32x core EPS against ~29% core EPS growth is roughly a 1.1x PEG on an accelerating, margin-expanding franchise — a full multiple, not an indefensible one, and the conservative seat never produced a peer or historical anchor to make "priced for perfection" bite.

The conservative and neutral seats nonetheless won the risk composition of the trade, and I adopt it. First, negative free cash flow is not a sentiment issue: TTM FCF is −$11.6B because capex reached $173.0B (+60.7% y/y), Q2 capex was $54.2B (~$217B annualized) and 27% of revenue, and — decisively — capex rose sequentially from $44.2B, which punctures the bull's "if capex merely flattens, FCF inflects" conditional and is why the RM's own catalyst list puts Q3 capex first. Capex is ~2.3x TTM D&A, so the depreciation bill is still ahead. Second, leverage is a trajectory problem: gross debt +92% to $132.2B in six months, interest expense +155% to $1.314B and a flip to net interest expense, quick ratio 0.875, $650B of contractual obligations with $78.1B due inside a year. It is not a solvency problem — +$30.4B net cash ex-leases, net debt including leases under five months of operating cash flow, and Q2 interest at roughly 5% of $27.5B operating income — but the conservative is right that we underwrite the direction, not the snapshot. Third, earnings quality: $62.8B of H1 mark-up takes GAAP EPS to $5.75 versus ~$2.16 core, and the $122.3B non-marketable equity book is ~11.2% of assets, self-marked with no disclosed inputs. The aggressive's "latent strategic value" framing cannot be counted as a free option while the reversal risk is discounted; the correct treatment is the RM's — underwrite core EPS ex-mark-up, which still grew ~29%, and treat any downward mark as a size-reduction event, not a dip to buy.

The neutral analyst won the decisive exchange on mechanics, and that is what turns this into Overweight rather than Buy. The 253.50 entry sits *below* the 50-SMA at 253.95, so it is a support test, not a confirmed defensive line — the aggressive's 3:1 and 12:1 payoff math assumes a held level that price has not yet proven. The 250.76 daily-close stop is only $2.74 from entry against ATR of 6.69, i.e. under half an average daily range, and AMZN has gapped double digits in this record (July 31), so a close-only stop bounds intent, not realized loss: size, not the stop, is the protection. And the 267.75 add into the 267.56 rejection high is an internal contradiction with trimming at the same zone — I strike that tranche and replace it with a breakout-and-retest add requiring fundamental confirmation. Capping at 0.75–1.0x until AWS and Q3 are verified is the conservative's best point; the neutral's objection to it — that AWS segment data and Q3 guidance are simply absent from the record, so making them a precondition is paralysis — is answered by staging rather than by refusing the trade.

Where the bear genuinely scores, and where all three seats agree, is the tape: AMZN at $258.51 sits below the 10-EMA (259.14), the VWMA (259.78) and the 20-SMA, under a resistance stack at 259.14–262.20, against lower highs of 287.20 → 278.84 → 267.56, with MACD only 0.339 above zero, RSI 49.55, and a 9/4 fade from a 261.12 high. Volume drying up into the low (24.0M on 9/2 vs 90.8M on 8/3) and three sessions of histogram improvement are early stabilization, not demand. But the primary trend is intact — price 8.11% above a rising 200-SMA at 239.12, a widening golden-cross spread, and the 50-SMA held on closes since 7/30 — so this is an entry-timing constraint, not a thesis break. That asymmetry is precisely why I start near 0.30x rather than chasing and finish only on confirmation.

Prior lessons applied: repeated AMZN de-risking inside an intact rising 50/200 structure (07-22 to 07-30) cost 12–22% of five-day alpha, and the 08-27 staged Overweight produced +0.8% alpha — so I will not over-de-risk a franchise growing core earnings ~29%; but the 08-18 lesson, that a constructive rating parked at a bad entry geometry is the recurring failure mode, and the 08-28 GOOGL lesson, that a de-risk trigger ~2–3% from spot should be acted on rather than held through, both argue for small committed size at the support edge plus explicit triggers rather than a full clip at mid-range.

What would change the call. Up to a full Buy / 1.25x add: Q3 capex flattening sequentially below $54.2B, D&A growth no longer outrunning revenue, core EPS ex-mark-up still compounding ~25%+, gross debt and interest expense no longer compounding, contract liabilities inflecting off ~$24.9B, and disclosed AWS segment revenue and margin. Down to Hold/Underweight: a daily close below 250.76 (stand down, no averaging), a close below 245.00 (reduce), continued capex escalation with capex-to-revenue still rising, total debt pushing past ~$150B, marketing as a percentage of revenue rising while margins stall, any markdown in the $122.3B equity book, or a Q3 print where the operating-margin expansion reverses while capex stays above $50B/quarter. Reduce to market weight into the Q2 2027 mark-up anniversary rather than holding a full Overweight through a potential ~60% like-for-like GAAP EPS air pocket. Explicit gaps, stated and not papered over: AWS segment revenue and margin cannot be verified from this record, no Q3 guidance or capex plan was supplied, no sentiment/positioning or insider data is in the run, and there is no portfolio, holdings or cash context — so all sizing is expressed as a fraction of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation, and AMZN should be counted as one AI-capex-correlated position alongside any existing NVDA or hyperscaler exposure. The Riverside strike and the DOJ beef review carry no sizing weight on the evidence presented.

**Price Target**: 274.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the Q3 print
